role_in_parent: Rewrites the reduced Gaussian quotient as the shifted product P_{a,b,r}(q).
statement_nl: For integers n, a, and b with 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n, define r := n - a - b. Then [n choose b]_q / [n choose a]_q = product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), where [n choose t]_q := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_t (q;q)_{n-t}), (q;q)_m := product_{j=1}^m (1 - q^j), (q;q)_0 := 1, and an empty product is interpreted as 1.

domain_restrictions: r = n - a - b, so r is a nonnegative integer
The q-binomial definition uses nonnegative integer inputs for the q-Pochhammer factors
The ratio is only meaningful when the denominator is nonzero, unless the identity is interpreted formally
The product from i = a + 1 to b is an empty product when a = b, and then it equals 1
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integers n, a, b satisfying 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n, if r is defined as n - a - b, then the quotient of the q-binomial coefficient of n choose b by the q-binomial coefficient of n choose a equals the finite product from i = a + 1 to b of (1 - q^(r + i)) divided by (1 - q^i), where the q-binomial coefficient is defined using the q-Pochhammer symbols and empty products are 1.
